anchor.title: Sits on a small chair on their own.

items.title: Inserts things like string into a small hole.
Walks down the stairs alone without holding on.
Forms playdough shapes (like an animal).
Takes steps using heel-to-toe motion.
When throwing, uses the body to aim (shifts weight, moves arm).
Can make quick turns while running, without falling or stopping.
Jumps down from a height of about 18 inches.
Runs with bent elbows.
Sorts things by their shape, like finding all the triangular blocks.
Understands when something is long or short.
Acts out stories following a clear order.
Mixes real and fantasy topics when talking.
Points to a triangle.
Identifies the sounds of musical instruments, like drums or guitar.
Makes up things or people in pretend play.
Names simple shapes like a circle, triangle, or square.

anchor.title: Says simple words with the letter B, like 'bye' or 'baby'.

items.title: Most people understand them when they speak.
Uses fingers to tell their age.
Answers simple questions about a story.
Uses sentences with at least five words.
Talks about their day.
Says plural words (like cars, dogs, and cats).
Names and describes their drawings.
Can chat using two to three sentences.

anchor.title: Knows that some things belong to them and some don't.

items.title: Puts their pants on.
Says their first and last name.
Likes playing with friends more than alone.
Can say their first name, age, and gender.
Shares their toys with other kids.
Can say who their friends are among kids they know.
Puts on shoes without laces.
Talks about what they are interested in.

calibration.title: Adapts speech tone for different situations (asks questions with rising tone, shows surprise).
Puts on a shirt without buttons.
